---
title: "Brokerage without bridging"
subtitle: "The middle class does not connect rich and poor in Brazilian cities"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# Everything quoted in the text below is computed here from data/derived/,
# so the page can never disagree with the data it is built from.
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = "data/derived"
ROLES = [  # (column suffix, label, endpoints share a stratum?)
    ("coordinator",            "coordinator — insider broker",   True),
    ("itinerant_above",        "itinerant — broker ranks above", True),
    ("itinerant_below",        "itinerant — broker ranks below", True),
    ("gatekeeper",             "gatekeeper",                     False),
    ("representative",         "representative",                 False),
    ("liaison_intermediate",   "liaison — intermediate broker",  False),
    ("liaison_extremal_above", "liaison — broker above both",    False),
    ("liaison_extremal_below", "liaison — broker below both",    False),
]
STRATS = [("gf_roles_population.csv", "equal-population", "#2A7F7A"),
          ("gf_roles_antenna.csv",    "equal-area",       "#C98A2E")]

tables = {}
for fname, label, _ in STRATS:
    p = os.path.join(DATA, fname)
    if os.path.exists(p):
        tables[label] = pd.read_csv(p)
pop = tables["equal-population"]

def vals(df, key):
    c = f"Rmix_{key}"
    return df[c].dropna() if c in df else pd.Series(dtype=float)

li = vals(pop, "liaison_intermediate")
n_li, k_li = len(li), int((li > 1).sum())
bridging = (f"none of the {n_li}" if k_li == 0 else f"{k_li} of the {n_li}")
same = pd.concat([vals(pop, k) for k, _, s in ROLES if s])
pct_same = 100 * float((same > 1).mean())
```

::: {.eyebrow}
Main result
:::

::: {.lede}
Whether city dwellers of different means come into contact depends on who stands
between them. We looked for those intermediaries in 3.1 billion mobile-phone calls
across nearly 300 Brazilian cities.
:::

::: {.finding}
**No stratum bridges the income poles.** No income group is over-represented on the
routes linking the poorest and the richest residents, and removing the middle class
cuts their reach to one another no more than removing the same number of people at
random.
:::

::: {.finding}
**Apparent elite gatekeeping is a volume effect.** The rich appear to control access to
their own group until the volume of contact between groups is held fixed. Then the
effect disappears, in every city and at both ends of the income distribution.
:::

::: {.finding}
**Intermediation is assortative.** Across every pair of income strata, residents broker
contact more often than chance only when the two people they connect belong to the same
stratum. The intermediate broker that the bridging account predicts is enriched in
`{python} bridging` cities.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-roles
#| fig-cap: "**Brokerage is enriched within strata and absent between them.** Enrichment of each brokerage role relative to a null model that holds fixed how much contact each income stratum exchanges. Points are medians across cities, bars the interquartile range. To the right of the dashed line a role occurs more often than chance. Two ways of dividing income into strata give the same picture."
#| fig-alt: "Dot plot of eight brokerage roles. The three roles whose endpoints share a stratum lie to the right of the chance line; the five roles connecting different strata, including the intermediate liaison, lie at or left of it."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 10,
                     "axes.edgecolor": "#4F5B61", "axes.labelcolor": "#1B2A33",
                     "xtick.color": "#4F5B61", "ytick.color": "#1B2A33"})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 4.9))
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAF7"); ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAF7")

ypos = {}
y = 0
for i, (key, label, same) in enumerate(ROLES):
    if i == 3:
        y += 1.3                                   # room for the second group header
    ypos[key] = y
    y += 1

offset = {"equal-population": -0.13, "equal-area": 0.13}
for fname, strat, colour in STRATS:
    if strat not in tables:
        continue
    for key, _, _ in ROLES:
        v = vals(tables[strat], key)
        if not len(v):
            continue
        q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(v, [25, 50, 75])
        yy = ypos[key] + offset[strat]
        ax.plot([q1, q3], [yy, yy], color=colour, lw=2.2, solid_capstyle="round")
        ax.plot(med, yy, "o", ms=7, color=colour,
                mfc=colour if strat == "equal-population" else "#FAFAF7", mew=1.8)

ax.axvline(1, color="#1B2A33", ls=(0, (4, 3)), lw=1)
ax.text(1.005, -1.05, "chance", color="#4F5B61", fontsize=9, va="center")
ax.set_yticks([ypos[k] for k, _, _ in ROLES])
ax.set_yticklabels([l for _, l, _ in ROLES])
for t, (key, _, _) in zip(ax.get_yticklabels(), ROLES):
    if key == "liaison_intermediate":
        t.set_fontweight("bold")                   # the bridging role
ax.set_xlabel("enrichment over chance, $R_\\mathrm{mix}$")
for side in ("top", "right", "left"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)

# group headers, right-aligned with the role labels, one row above each group
for first, text in (("coordinator", "THE TWO CONNECTED PEOPLE SHARE A STRATUM"),
                    ("gatekeeper", "THE TWO CONNECTED PEOPLE ARE IN DIFFERENT STRATA")):
    ax.text(-0.02, ypos[first] - 1.0, text, transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),
            ha="right", va="center", fontsize=8, color="#C98A2E", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylim(y - 0.4, -1.6)                         # inverted: top headroom for headers

handles = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", color=c, mfc=c if s == "equal-population" else "#FAFAF7",
                  mew=1.8, lw=2.2, label=s) for _, s, c in STRATS if s in tables]
ax.legend(handles=handles, frameon=False, loc="lower right", fontsize=9,
          title="income strata", title_fontsize=9)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.40, right=0.97, top=0.98, bottom=0.12)
plt.show()
```

## What this means for cities

Research on urban segregation has moved from where people live to where they go and
whom they encounter. This result adds a further layer: how contact is arranged.
Residents of these cities do call across class lines --- most two-step chains of contact
link people in different income strata --- but no stratum occupies the positions that
would carry interaction from one class to the next. A city can therefore look integrated
by exposure, or even by its share of cross-class ties, while remaining divided in how
those ties are mediated.
